paper_title: Linear Coupling: An Ultimate Unification of Gradient and Mirror Descent
statement: 5 Beyond Accelerated Gradient Methods Providing an intuitive, yet complete interpretation of accelerated gradient methods is an open question in Optimization [17]. Our result in this paper is one important step towards this general goal. Linear coupling not only gives a reinterpretation of Nesterov’s accelerated methods, more importantly, it provides a framework for designing first-order methods in a bigger agenda. Since the original version of this paper appeared online, our linear-coupling framework has led to breakthroughs for several problems in computer science. In all such problems, the original Nesterov’s accelerated methods do not apply. We illustrate a few examples in this line of research, in order to demonstrate the power and generality of linear coupling.

AGM is slightly different from [27]: (1) we use Nemirovski’s mirror steps instead of dual 2 averaging steps, (2) we allow arbitrary starting points x0 , and (3) we use τk = k+2 rather 2 than τk = k+3 . AGM is very different from the perhaps better-known version [26], which is known by some authors as the “momentum method” [32, 41]. Momentum methods do not apply to non-Euclidean settings. In Appendix D, we also recover the strong convexity version of accelerated gradient methods [26], and thus linear coupling provides a complete proof of all existing accelerated gradient methods. 5 Beyond Accelerated Gradient Methods Providing an intuitive, yet complete interpretation of accelerated gradient methods is an open question in Optimization [17]. Our result in this paper is one important step towards this general goal. Linear coupling not only gives a reinterpretation of Nesterov’s accelerated methods, more importantly, it provides a framework for designing first-order methods in a bigger agenda. Since the original version of this paper appeared online, our linear-coupling framework has led to breakthroughs for several problems in computer science. In all such problems, the original Nesterov’s accelerated methods do not apply. We illustrate a few examples in this line of research, in order to demonstrate the power and generality of linear coupling.
